items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: work another place for a Mr. Steinberg

ctx.x: I don't know. Never did -- nobody just

never recorded him. Should have, because he's had the bands. And so I stayed with his band. We were in -- we were working in Seminole and there was a ballroom in Tulsa that we used to work like two months at a time and we'd go to Oklahoma City and work another place for a Mr. Steinberg, work two months and the name of that one, one in Tulsa, was Casa Loma Ballroom, beautiful ballroom, and the one in Tulsa was -- I mean in Oklahoma City was Spring Lake. That's where we were working when I caught King Oliver.

Anyway, but then we'd go down to Seminole -- that's between Oklahoma City and Tulsa -- a lot of money, nothing but money, oil and hustlers and everything and money. Everybody spending plenty of money. We made $75.00 a week for three days in 1930. That was a lot of money. So we got a saxophone player that loved Frankie Trumbauer, looked like Frankie Trumbauer, very light skin, looked like Frankie Trumbauer, but he was so -- could play, pretty sound and everything, and we had a lot of hard reed choruses in those…
